_about: Every player setting and where it sits in the menus: sections > pages (sub-menus) > groups > items. Settings (scripts/core/settings.gd) takes defaults from here and saves changes to user://settings.cfg; the settings screen is drawn from this file, so a new setting is one item here plus the code that reads it. Item types: choice (options as [value, label] pairs, or options_from a registry), toggle, slider (min, max, step, format), keybinds (a generated bindings table for a scheme), button (runs an action), info (text only). "preset_field" ties a graphics item to graphics_presets.json. "visible_if" hides an item or page until a toggle is on. "generate": "audio_buses" makes one volume slider per bus in sounds.json. Formats: percent, x, deg, m, s, int, float, db.

items.label: Quality preset
items.help: Low aims for 60 fps on this laptop, Medium 45, High 30. Ultra is for stronger hardware. Changing any single setting below makes this Custom.

items.label: Window
items.help: Fullscreen gives the steadiest frame pacing.

items.label: Vertical sync
items.help: Off shows the true frame rate but can tear.

items.label: Frame rate cap
items.help: A cap below what the laptop can hold keeps it cooler and smoother.

items.label: Render resolution
items.help: The 3D scene renders at this share of the screen and is scaled up. Menus and the HUD stay sharp.

items.label: Upscaler
items.help: How the lower render resolution is scaled to the screen. FSR 2 also smooths edges but costs more.

items.label: Sharpening
items.help: Extra crispness from the FSR 1 upscaler. High values make ground and foliage look grainy; 0% keeps the upscale smooth.

items.label: Brightness
items.help: Scene brightness. Menus are not affected.

items.label: Frame rate counter
options: Frames per second and frame time
items.help: F3 toggles it in game.

items.label: Bounced light (SDFGI)
items.help: Light bouncing off terrain and walls. Beautiful and expensive.

items.label: Screen-space bounce light
items.help: Fine local bounce light from what is on screen.

items.label: Sun shadow resolution
items.help: Sharper sun shadows cost video memory and time.

items.label: Shadow softness
items.help: Softer shadow edges take more samples.

items.label: Shadow distance
items.help: How far away things still cast sun shadows.

items.label: Ambient occlusion
items.help: Contact shadows in creases and under the mech.

items.label: Ambient occlusion quality
items.help: Finer, steadier contact shadows cost more. Very low is about half the cost of Medium.

items.label: Screen-space reflections
items.help: Reflections on water and wet metal from what is on screen.

items.label: Volumetric fog
items.help: Light shafts and fog that the sun and lamps light up.

items.label: Fog detail (width)
items.help: Fog grid resolution across the screen.

items.label: Fog detail (depth)
items.help: Fog grid slices into the distance.

items.label: Clouds
items.help: Volumetric cloud quality (maps from lane B3 on).

items.label: Glow
items.help: Bloom on bright muzzle flashes, lamps and the sun.

items.label: Multisample AA
items.help: Clean geometry edges. Costly on this GPU.

items.label: Screen AA
items.help: Smooths edges after the frame is drawn.

items.label: Texture filtering
items.help: Keeps ground textures sharp at shallow angles.

items.label: Draw distance
items.help: How far the world is drawn.

items.label: Model detail threshold
items.help: Lower keeps full-detail models further away.

items.label: Grass and shrub density
items.help: Share of scattered grass, shrubs and small rocks drawn.

items.label: Dust from the feet
items.help: Each foot throws a puff of dust at a run, more the faster you go; less on rock, none on steel.

items.label: Scorch marks kept
items.help: How many shell scorches and wall cracks stay on the map before the oldest fade out (bullet holes keep three quarters as many).

items.label: Shell hit size
items.help: How big a shell's hit looks: an HE or HEAT shell's fireball, flash and thrown dirt, and the dirt a 57 mm dart kicks up off the ground. Look only: damage and push stay as the ammo data sets them. 1.0x is the old size (the fireball and thrown dirt are new at any size).

items.label: Hit dust
items.help: How big the dust from hits on the ground and buildings grows and how long it hangs in the air, from bullets to shells and collapsing buildings. 1.0x is the old size (the fireball and thrown dirt are new at any size).

items.label: Shell tracers
items.help: How the 57 mm and other shells' tracers look in flight, so you can follow a round to where it lands. Bright is three times as thick and glows, with a faint trail behind. Look only.

items.label: Bindings
items.help: Pick a slot, then press the new key, mouse button or pad button. Escape cancels, Delete clears the slot.

items.label: Reset standard bindings
items.help: Puts every standard binding back to its default.

items.label: Inner dead zone
items.help: Stick movement inside this is ignored (stops drift).

items.label: Outer dead zone
items.help: Past this the stick counts as fully pushed.

items.label: Response curve
items.help: 1 is linear. Higher gives finer control near the centre, lower gives a quicker start.

items.label: Inner dead zone
items.help: Stick movement inside this is ignored.

items.label: Outer dead zone
items.help: Past this the stick counts as fully pushed.

items.label: Response curve
items.help: Higher makes small aim corrections easier.

items.label: Turn speed
items.help: Scales how fast the stick turns the chassis.

items.label: Invert body tilt
items.help: Push up to tilt the body down.

items.label: Trigger dead zone
items.help: Trigger travel ignored at the top.

items.label: Trigger full at
items.help: Past this the trigger counts as fully pulled.

items.label: Trigger curve
items.help: Shapes analog brake and throttle feel.

items.label: Fire point
items.help: How far R2 must be pulled to fire.

items.label: Mouse moves
options: The chassis (turn and tilt to aim)
items.help: Steer is the usual way to fight: the gun is fixed, so the mouse turns the whole machine.

items.label: Sensitivity
items.help: How far the chassis turns per mouse movement.

items.label: Invert vertical
items.help: Move the mouse up to tilt down.

items.label: Smoothing
items.help: Averages mouse movement over a few frames; the chassis is heavy anyway.

items.label: Throttle ramp
items.help: How long a held movement key takes to reach full throttle, so keys feel less like a switch.

items.label: Run button
items.help: Toggle: press once to run until you stop.

items.label: Crouch button
items.help: Jump is always hold-to-charge.

items.label: Rumble
items.help: Controller vibration.

items.label: Overall strength
items.help: Scales every rumble.

items.label: Weapons
items.help: Gun fire and reloads.

items.label: Footsteps and movement
items.help: Footfalls, jumps, landings, skids and the wire.

items.label: Hits and near misses
items.help: Taking hits and shell wakes.

items.label: Menus
items.help: Small ticks when you confirm or go back.

items.label: Test rumble
items.help: Plays the main gun pattern on every connected pad.

items.label: Adaptive triggers and speaker
items.text: Lane B4 reports whether Godot can reach these on Linux.
items.help: Research only in this wave.

items.label: Hardcore manual walking
items.help: Steel Battalion meets QWOP: each leg lifts on its own button and the right stick or mouse shifts your weight. Step in rhythm and keep balanced or you tip over. Unlocks its own bindings page.

items.label: Bindings
items.help: The manual-walking layout. Clashes are only checked inside this layout.

items.label: Reset hardcore bindings
items.help: Puts every hardcore binding back to its default.

items.label: Main menu
items.help: The music on the menus. Soundtrack plays the 86 soundtrack album through in order, carrying on where it left off; Shuffle picks from the tracks marked for menus; or pick one track.

items.label: Exploring
items.help: The music while you walk the map with no Legion near. Soundtrack plays the album through in order.

items.label: In combat
items.help: The music once you fire or are fired on; it fades back to exploring after a quiet spell. With Soundtrack in both, the album just carries on.

items.label: Song language
items.help: For Shuffle: only songs in this language (instrumental score always counts).

items.label: Extra tracks
items.help: Also offer the English covers and the soundtrack preview reel. Off: only the soundtrack and one original version of each opening and ending.

items.label: Next track
items.help: Jump to another track now.

items.label: Output device
items.help: Where the sound goes.

items.label: Listening on
items.help: Tunes panning and reverb for what you listen on (lane B4).

items.label: Dynamic range
items.help: Night squashes gunfire and explosions so you can keep it quiet.

items.label: Mute when in the background
items.help: Silence the game when another window has focus.

items.label: Starting view
items.help: Which view a mission starts in.

items.label: Third-person field of view
items.help: Vertical field of view.

items.label: Cockpit field of view
items.help: Vertical field of view inside the cockpit.

items.label: Cockpit view from
items.help: A Juggernaut pilot sees out through the optical sensor at the front of the pod. The pilot seat sits under the 57 mm, so the barrel and front plates fill the view.

items.label: Camera distance
items.help: How far behind the Juggernaut the camera sits.

items.label: Camera weight
items.help: How much the camera lags and settles behind the chassis.

items.label: Camera shake
items.help: Shake from footfalls, firing and hits.

items.label: Cockpit head movement
items.help: How much the pilot's view rocks with each step.

items.label: HUD size
items.help: Scales the in-game readouts.

items.label: HUD opacity
items.help: How solid the readouts are.

items.label: Gun reticle
items.help: The 57 mm's own mark: where its round would land along the bore line (drop included), with the range. The 57 mm is fixed to the body: turn and tilt the body to move it.

items.label: Sub-arm guns
options: Fixed straight ahead on the body
A little play on the mounts
items.help: Fixed: the 12.7 mm guns point where the body points, like the 57 mm. A little play: each mount swings a few degrees toward your aim. Aimed by the arms: the sub-arms swing the guns onto your aim within their reach. Their mark is the small cross.

items.label: Move hints
items.help: A short hint the first time a move is possible (the gallop, the slide, a flip, the wire anchor, the air). Each shows once, ever.

items.label: Heading tape
items.help: Compass strip at the top of the screen.

items.label: Objective guide
items.help: Shows the distance and compass bearing to the nearest Legion of the current wave, under the objective and as a diamond on the heading tape.

items.label: Damage diagram
items.help: Per-part health of your Juggernaut.

items.label: Units
items.help: Speeds and ranges.

items.label: Damage you take
items.help: Scales Legion weapon damage.

items.label: Damage you deal
items.help: Scales your weapon damage.

items.label: Permanent part damage
items.help: Lost armour and hurt legs stay that way for the whole mission.

items.label: Reserve ammunition
items.help: Magazines still need reloading either way.

items.label: Allied Juggernauts
items.help: How many of the squad (Werewolf, Laughing Fox, Gunslinger, Snow Witch) deploy beside you. Each is a full physics Juggernaut, so more of them cost frame rate. Order them with 1 follow, 2 hold, 3 attack, 4 regroup, or from the Handler view (Tab). Takes effect at the next mission start.

items.label: Physics mode
items.help: Game mode uses strong magic motors. Test bench uses real electric actuator limits: slow, power-hungry and hot. The bench settings are in the group below.

items.label: Balance assist
items.help: A gentle helper that keeps the chassis level. Off is harder.

items.label: Body tilts to aim
items.help: Up and down on the mouse or right stick leans the whole chassis on its legs (and pitches it in the air) to aim the fixed gun. Off keeps everything level.

items.label: Aiming
items.help: How up and down on the right stick moves the aim. Rate: holding it keeps tilting until you let go, and the aim stays where you left it. Angle: how far you push is the angle (all the way up is the top of the range, half is half) and letting go springs back level. The mouse works the same in both. Mid-air the body only tilts as far as the swinging legs can turn it.

items.label: Leg-swing turning in the air
items.help: In the air the legs swing and tuck to turn the body toward your aim, the way a cat turns as it falls: real physics, so it is slow (4 to 6 degrees a second). Nothing pushes you in flight: steer with the main gun's recoil and the wire anchor. Off keeps the legs still.

groups.label: Test bench (lane B6; needs Physics mode: Test bench)

items.label: Design on the bench
items.help: Which mech the two test bench maps load: a Blender export with the actuator figures from parts.json. Takes effect when a bench map starts.

items.label: Failures
items.help: A winding that gets too hot trips its thermal cutout, and a shock load past what a joint can take breaks it until you reset the bench. Off: the torque limits and heat still apply but nothing latches.

items.label: Cooling
items.help: Scales how fast the actuators shed heat. Lower makes them overheat sooner.

items.label: Battery size
items.help: Pack capacity in kilowatt hours.

items.label: Charge at reset
items.help: How full the pack is when the bench starts or is reset.

items.label: Bench readouts
items.help: Torque, power, temperature and failures per joint, and the battery and bus.

items.label: Slide friction
items.help: How hard the feet grip while sliding (steel on dirt is about 0.4). Lower slides longer and turns the path less; higher bites harder and stops sooner.

items.label: Slide turn rate
items.help: How fast the body can spin round in a full slide, at full turn input. Less input turns less: none at all is a pure sideways drift.

items.label: Flip turns
items.help: Hold crouch as you let go of a charged jump and the stick picks a flip (forward: front flip, back: backflip, sideways: side flip). The flight computer leans the launch push onto the feet that way just enough to turn this many times before landing, with the stick fully pushed; less stick, less turn. In the air, hold crouch to tuck the legs and spin faster; let go to open up and slow down.

items.label: Flip lean limit
items.help: How far toward the furthest grounded foot the push may move for a flip. 100% lets the whole push go through that foot when a flip needs it; 0% turns flips off.

items.label: Show the wire anchor's arc
items.help: Dots show the path the anchor dart will fly (it falls and slows as it pulls its line): pale where it will bite, red where it cannot. The launcher already lifts its aim so the dart lands on the crosshair.

items.label: Winch size
items.help: How big a winch drives the wire anchors. Its pull and power draw scale together and the rope is sized up with it so it never out-pulls its own line; a heavier rope makes the dart drop a little sooner. 1.4x is 336 kN of pull and 420 kW (1x: 240 kN, 300 kW).

items.label: Ride height
items.help: Raises the body on its legs, so the legs stand steeper. 0 is the modelled pose.

items.label: Foot spread
items.help: How far out the feet stand from the hip joints. Lower is a narrower, steeper stance; 1 is the modelled pose.

items.label: Leg length
items.help: Stretches the thighs and shins (look, reach and hitboxes together). 1 is the modelled length.

items.label: Mech finish
items.help: Paint and wear on your Juggernaut: field worn, fresh from the hangar, or the bare model export.

items.label: Legion livery
items.help: How the Legion are painted: field worn (dirty cream chipped to dark metal, red eyes), night (clean silver-blue liquid metal) or the bare model export.

items.label: Dirt builds up
items.help: Your Juggernaut gets dustier over a sortie: running on dirt (more at speed), hard landings and skids. Each new sortie starts at the finish's own wear; off washes it.

items.label: Emblem
items.help: The personal mark painted on both sides of the cockpit. Undertaker is Shin's headless skeleton with its shovel.

items.label: Metal shine
items.help: How mirror-like the metal is. 100% is the chosen finish as painted.

items.label: Menu theme
items.help: Switches straight away.

items.label: Button prompts
items.help: Which buttons the game shows in hints.

items.label: Menu sounds
items.help: Clicks and ticks in menus.

items.label: Juggernaut behind the menu
items.help: The main menu shows your Juggernaut standing in the hangar behind the buttons, swaying slowly. Off draws the plain menu backdrop (a little lighter on the laptop).

items.label: Hangar lighting
items.help: The light the Juggernaut is shown in, in the Hangar and behind the main menu. Also changes with Q and E in the Hangar.

items.label: Tutorial hints
items.help: A stub for now: off by default until Emerson decides after testing.

items.label: Menu and text size
items.help: Scales menus and text.

items.label: High contrast menus
items.help: Brighter text and solid panels.

items.label: Colour filter
items.help: Shifts colours so red, green and blue cues stay apart.

items.label: Filter strength
items.help: How strongly the filter applies.

items.label: Reduce motion
items.help: Cuts camera shake and cockpit head movement.

items.label: Reduce flashing
items.help: Dims muzzle flashes and explosions.

items.label: Subtitles
items.help: Radio and voice lines as text.

items.label: Subtitle size
items.help: Text size of subtitles.

items.label: Subtitle background
items.help: Darkness of the box behind subtitles.

items.label: Speaker names
items.help: Show who is talking.
